Download the Data

The same three files posted with the article's replication package, trimmed to the variables used in the published analysis, as CSV. Each download asks you to confirm before saving.

Candidates, 1980–2024

One row per major-party candidate who filed with the FEC: prior elected experience, primary participation and outcomes under each candidate-pool definition, pre-primary fundraising share, covariates.

6,595 rows × 25 variables · CSV

Party primaries, 1980–2024

One row per major-party Senate primary: nomination type, primary rules, seat status, counts of emerging and on-ballot candidates by experience, state co-partisanship.

1,596 rows × 20 variables · CSV

General-election races, 1914–2024

Senate general elections with the Democratic two-party vote share and the prior elected experience of each party's nominee.

1,976 rows × 8 variables · CSV

About the Data

Draft for coauthor review

The Rise of Amateur Candidate Pipelines & Declining Value of Candidate Experience in U.S. Senate Primaries, 1980–2024

Authors: Carlos Algara, Byengseon Bae, Isaac Hale, Michael Heseltine, and Evan Lieber. Legislative Studies Quarterly.

These are the cleaned analysis data behind the article: every major-party candidate who filed with the Federal Election Commission for the U.S. Senate from 1980 to 2024, coded for most recent prior elected office, primary participation and outcomes, and pre-primary fundraising; a primary-level file with candidate counts; and a general-election file (1914–2024) with nominee experience.

A quality candidate is one who has previously held elected office of any kind. Candidates with no prior elected office are coded Amateur.

Charts on this page are descriptive summaries of the posted data. The article's model-based estimates (Figures 4–7 and the appendix) are reproduced by the replication code on Dataverse. This page is a static preview of a fuller Shiny application that adds filters by primary type, year range and state, and RDS downloads.
